items.exact_question: When a hard battery-SOC-floor violation (or other verified safety finding) is detected, what specific automatic or operator-facing action must occur BEFORE the system is allowed to halt dispatch? items.why_it_matters: No safe-response mechanism exists anywhere in the codebase today (confirmed by search of system/safety, system/control, system/simulation). Per the owner's own Policy A, halting is only authorized AFTER safe-response handling; without this definition, no halt can ever be legitimately wired in, and every safety finding today is purely diagnostic.
items.current_documented_policy: Policy A requires halt only after safe-response; SAFETY_ENFORCEMENT_AUDIT_AND_PROPOSAL.md Section 3 case 1 confirms no such mechanism exists and declines to invent one.

significance_criterion_trace_2026_10_17.task: Trace the p<0.05 vs. p<0.01 significance-criterion discrepancy flagged in N6_ANNOTATION_AND_EVIDENCE_PLANNING_REPORT.md Section 2 (last paragraph) through source, per this pass's directive item 2.
significance_criterion_trace_2026_10_17.finding: These are TWO DIFFERENT, independently-authored criteria governing two different decision points, not one requirement stated inconsistently in two places. (1) DIESEL_REDUCTION_CONTROL_DESIGN.md:205 states the PREREGISTERED EXPERIMENT-ACCEPTANCE TEST for DSL-01's own Candidate-2 123-origin evaluation: 'Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank, two-sided p < 0.05 AND BCa 95% CI for mean fuel saving ... strictly > 0' -- no percentage-savings floor is attached to this criterion. (2) system/safety/reserve_policy_guard.py:98-103's SAFETY_GATE_REGISTRY['diesel_savings_significance'] defines a SEPARATE, textually unrelated, still-unauthorized (authorized=False) SAF-05 production-PROMOTION gate: 'Diesel savings must exceed 2% with p < 0.01.' Neither document cites, cross-references, or supersedes the other. Chronologically, DIESEL_REDUCTION_CONTROL_DESIGN.md (2026-10-05 15:52) predates reserve_policy_guard.py (2026-10-17 14:11) by 12 days; grep of reserve_policy_guard.py found zero references to DIESEL_REDUCTION_CONTROL_DESIGN.md, DSL-01, or epsilon_tol, and grep of DIESEL_REDUCTION_CONTROL_DESIGN.md found zero references to a 2% floor or p<0.01. SAF-05's own proposed_threshold_note independently confirms its p<0.01 gate is 'proposed in prior audit, not formally authorized' -- i.e. it was never claimed to be the same decision as DSL-01's own preregistered test.
significance_criterion_trace_2026_10_17.why_no_resolution_exists: No document in the repository states that these two p-values must be equal, that one supersedes the other, or that a production-promotion gate is intentionally stricter than its own feeding research experiment's acceptance test. A plausible, but UNCONFIRMED, reading is that SAF-05's p<0.01 is a deliberately tighter bar layered on top of DSL-01's own p<0.05 experiment result before that result may be used for production promotion (a common two-tier pattern: looser bar to call an experiment's own result 'significant,' stricter bar before acting on it). This reading is NOT invented or adopted as a resolution here -- it is reported as one possible, unconfirmed interpretation, per the directive's explicit instruction not to pick a value or close an inconsistency without an unambiguous governing source.
significance_criterion_trace_2026_10_17.action_taken_this_pass: No value was selected, invented, or reconciled. DIESEL_REDUCTION_CONTROL_DESIGN.md and system/safety/reserve_policy_guard.py were both read-only this pass; neither was edited. DSL-01's own disposition (OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED, epsilon_tol unresolved) is UNCHANGED by this finding -- epsilon_tol (a critical-reliability threshold) and the significance criterion (a p-value) are different quantities; this trace does not close DSL-01, it only clarifies that the p<0.05/p<0.01 'discrepancy' the prior planning pass flagged as needing reconciliation is better understood as two distinct, non-conflicting criteria for two distinct decisions -- unless the owner says otherwise.
significance_criterion_trace_2026_10_17.narrowly_scoped_owner_decision_needed: Confirm whether (a) DIESEL_REDUCTION_CONTROL_DESIGN.md's p<0.05 (DSL-01's own research-experiment acceptance test) and reserve_policy_guard.py's p<0.01 (SAF-05's separate, still-unauthorized production-promotion gate) are intentionally two distinct, both-standing criteria for two distinct decision points, as this trace concludes is the more likely reading -- in which case no correction is needed to either file; or (b) the owner instead intends a single, unified diesel-reduction significance level, in which case the owner must state which value (0.05 or 0.01) governs and whether reserve_policy_guard.py's registry entry or DIESEL_REDUCTION_CONTROL_DESIGN.md's preregistration should be corrected to match. This pass does not assume (a) is the final answer -- it is reported as the evidence-supported default reading pending the owner's confirmation.
significance_criterion_trace_2026_10_17.boundary_confirmation: Does not authorize Candidate 2, does not invent or select epsilon_tol, and does not edit any safety-gate threshold or diesel-reduction design document.

owner_decision_note_2026_10_17.purpose: Concise owner decision note for epsilon_tol, per directive item 3 this pass. Does not select a value.
owner_decision_note_2026_10_17.what_the_threshold_controls: epsilon_tol is DSL-01's own preregistered critical-reliability ACCEPTANCE threshold: the maximum tolerable degradation in critical-load service (however defined -- e.g. unmet critical energy, critical service ratio) that Candidate 2 (Net-Deficit EBR, Variant S/SW) may exhibit relative to baseline/Control before its 123-origin research evaluation is considered to have passed. It is DISTINCT from: (a) the diesel-savings significance criterion (p<0.05 research test vs. p<0.01 SAF-05 production gate -- see significance_criterion_trace_2026_10_17 below, a separate traced-but-unresolved question), and (b) SAF-03's reserve-shortfall ceiling / SAF-04's solar-credit cap (EBR/dispatch-level quantities, not a candidate-acceptance threshold).
owner_decision_note_2026_10_17.existing_reliability_metrics_and_methodo: DIESEL_REDUCTION_CONTROL_DESIGN.md's preregistered protocol (2026-10-05) specifies a 123-origin paired evaluation using: (1) a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (two-sided) on fuel savings between Candidate 2 and baseline, with significance read at p<0.05; (2) a 95% BCa bootstrap confidence interval for the mean fuel saving, required to lie strictly above 0; (3) exact research-defined critical-load metrics (consuming the CL-01-settled 11,600 W provisional synthetic demand value). No epsilon_tol (critical-reliability degradation ceiling) is itself defined anywhere in this protocol or any other repository document found this pass or any prior pass.
owner_decision_note_2026_10_17.evidence_needed_to_compare_candidate_thr: A candidate epsilon_tol value could only be meaningfully compared against alternatives using: (a) the actual, replay-measured distribution of critical-load-service degradation Candidate 2 produces across the 123 origins (requires executing the preregistered evaluation itself -- gated behind a SEPARATE execution authorization and CampaignExecutionNotAuthorizedError, NOT performed this pass or any prior pass); (b) a real (non-synthetic) Nuolja critical-load baseline against which 'degradation' is measured (EVID-02, still NOT_ESTABLISHED); (c) the owner's own stated risk tolerance for critical-service degradation, which no repository evidence can supply -- this is irreducibly an owner judgment, not a derivable statistic, similar to SAF-03/04's own numeric ceilings.

Leaving epsilon_tol unset indefinitely means the fully-corrected Candidate 2 design remains unused research output; it does not create any safety risk by itself (no execution occurs without it), but it does block all further progress on the diesel-reduction research track.
